subject: Civil Engineering
title: Box Girder Bridges: Hollow Strength
description: A 60-second lesson on Box Girder Bridges: Hollow Strength.

hook.text: Slice open a modern highway bridge and you'll find a hollow box, not a solid beam.

buildup.text: Box girders are closed sections — top, bottom, and side walls form a tube.

discovery.text: The closed shape resists twisting far better than an open I-beam.

twist.text: Curved highway ramps need torsion resistance — only box girders deliver it.

climax.text: Segmental box girders are built piece by piece, like Lego, from both ends.

punchline.text: Hollow boxes twist less, weigh less, and span farther.

quiz.question: Why are box girders preferred for curved highway ramps?
options: They look better than I-beams on curved paths
Their closed shape resists the twisting forces that curves generate
They are less expensive than any other girder type

details.summary: Box girder bridges use hollow rectangular or trapezoidal cross-sections that provide excellent resistance to bending, shear, and torsion. The closed box shape is particularly effective for curved alignments and long-span viaducts because it resists twisting forces far better than open I-sections.
details.whyItMatters: Box girders dominate modern highway and railway viaduct construction. Their ability to resist torsion makes them essential for curved roads and bridges carrying off-center loads.
takeaways: The closed box shape resists torsion far better than open I-sections
Box girders are ideal for curved highway alignments
They can be built by segmental construction, launching, or incremental pushing

faq.question: Why is a hollow box stronger in torsion than a solid section?
faq.answer: Torsion resistance depends on the enclosed area of the cross-section. A hollow box encloses a large area while using material efficiently at the perimeter where shear stresses are highest. A solid section concentrates material at the center where it contributes less to torsion resistance.

faq.question: How are long box girder viaducts constructed?
faq.answer: Common methods include balanced cantilever construction where segments are added from both sides of each pier, incremental launching where the girder is pushed forward from one end, and precast segmental construction where factory-made segments are lifted and glued into position.
